editorial_thesis: Agent systems are becoming durable workflows with memory, identity, and evidence; today’s practical edge is bounded, inspectable orchestration rather than raw autonomy.

topic_groups.title: Agentic Delivery Surfaces
topic_groups.selection_rationale: A clear product shift is making orchestration, session continuity, and task-shaped interfaces first-class; this is new practical signal after recent runtime-focused coverage.

sources.title: GitHub Universe 2026: Evolving every layer of the stack
sources.why_selected: Agentic delivery now spans ideation, planning, implementation, verification, deployment, and continuous learning.
sources.usefulness: Use as a reference for Buildn’s “brief → run → evidence → review” spine.

sources.title: Dynamic workflows in Copilot CLI and the Copilot app
sources.why_selected: Code-defined orchestration combines deterministic steps, agents, structured handoffs, parallel work, checkpoints, and resume.
sources.usefulness: Prototype a reusable dossier-research workflow with typed outputs and a review pause.

sources.title: When chat is the wrong UI
sources.why_selected: Task-shaped canvases can expose state and controls more clearly than a transcript.
sources.usefulness: Test a visual run board for evidence, approvals, and next actions.

sources.title: GitHub Copilot SDK
sources.why_selected: An SDK surface makes agent capabilities embeddable in custom developer workflows rather than trapped in the CLI.
sources.usefulness: Compare the SDK boundary with Hermes tool registration and session state.

sources.title: Copilot automations
sources.why_selected: Repo-native automations point toward agents triggered by events, not only prompts.
sources.usefulness: Use event triggers for recurring evidence checks or release hygiene.

topic_groups.title: Evidence-Linked Agent Memory
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Memory has been under-covered relative to infrastructure and security, and two current research signals make the practical design rule sharper: memory must learn from experience and remain auditable.

sources.title: The Sleep Framework: Continual Learning for LLMs
sources.why_selected: Google Research separates active interaction from offline consolidation, using a periodic sleep phase to stabilize new knowledge.
sources.usefulness: Borrow the wake/sleep split for ingest: collect during the day, consolidate only after review.

sources.title: ReasoningBank: Enabling agents to learn from experience
sources.why_selected: Successful and failed trajectories are distilled into reusable reasoning strategies, not copied as raw traces.
sources.usefulness: Turn failed client runs into preventative playbooks, linked to the original evidence.

sources.title: Don’t Just Trust Your Memory
sources.why_selected: WikiTrace links each lesson to a compilation and the unchanged raw trajectory; reported results reduce memory-induced regressions.
sources.usefulness: Make every Buildn memory item clickable back to source notes, artifacts, and decisions.

sources.title: Continual Learning Exam
sources.why_selected: CLE tests five-level professional task ladders and whether experience improves later work; frontier systems still struggle with sustained learning.
sources.usefulness: Use sequential client scenarios rather than isolated prompt tests.

sources.title: AgentCL: Toward Rigorous Evaluation of Continual Learning
sources.why_selected: AgentCL compares memory designs across retrieval, test-time learning, and continual adaptation settings.
sources.usefulness: Use its taxonomy to separate retrieval quality from genuine skill improvement.

topic_groups.title: Agent Identity + Interoperability
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Security coverage has recently emphasized detection and runtime controls; today’s gap is the control-plane question: who is the agent, what authority was delegated, and how can systems interoperate safely?

sources.title: SI Agent Standards Initiative
sources.why_selected: NIST is organizing work around trusted, interoperable, secure autonomous agents, including identity infrastructure and multi-agent security.
sources.usefulness: Use the pillars as a client-readiness checklist and a Buildn authority model.

sources.title: Software and AI Agent Identity and Authorization
sources.why_selected: NCCoE connects agent identity and authorization to enterprise use cases and existing identity standards.
sources.usefulness: Separate human identity, agent identity, delegated authority, and tool scopes.

sources.title: Announcing the AI Agent Standards Initiative
sources.why_selected: The initiative frames interoperability and secure action on behalf of users as adoption prerequisites.
sources.usefulness: Use as a source for client education and non-hype positioning.

sources.title: Open and Emergent Problems in Agentic Privacy and Security
sources.why_selected: Privacy risk depends on context, tool access, and the social setting in which agents act, not only model behavior.
sources.usefulness: Add context and purpose to tool authorization reviews.

sources.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications 2026
sources.why_selected: Goal hijack, tool misuse, and related classes translate agent risk into test fixtures.
sources.usefulness: Build adversarial fixtures around authority escalation and unintended tool use.

topic_groups.title: Physical-Agent Evaluation
topic_groups.selection_rationale: Physical AI is a deliberate coverage gap after several software-agent runs. RLE-Bench and CLE together show how to evaluate agents on heterogeneous artifacts, constraints, and learning over time.

sources.title: RLE-Bench: Can Your AI Engineer a Robot?
sources.why_selected: Harvard and Georgia Tech’s open benchmark covers 48 tasks across control, policy, perception, and mechanical design.
sources.usefulness: Borrow capability profiles instead of one “agent score” for complex delivery work.

sources.title: RLE-Bench paper
sources.why_selected: The benchmark scores workflow-specific artifacts and aggregates them into an overall index plus capability profiles.
sources.usefulness: Use artifact-level scoring for plans, code, evidence, and decisions.

sources.title: RLE-Bench project site
sources.why_selected: The public project makes the benchmark and task structure accessible for inspection and reuse.
sources.usefulness: Review task packaging as a model for reproducible agent evaluations.

sources.title: Continual Learning Exam
sources.why_selected: Five-level task ladders test whether an agent retains and applies experience across professional work.
sources.usefulness: Combine capability slices with sequential progression in client pilots.

sources.title: Embodied First Exam
sources.why_selected: A broad evaluation combines many capability and safety suites rather than a single narrow benchmark.
sources.usefulness: Use a multi-surface evidence pack for any agent touching real operations.
